(Ahlqvist et al., 2020). Recent efforts have proposed phenotype-based approaches that take advantage of modern computational
capabilities and clustering techniques. These strategies have the potential to highlight underlying disease pathophysiology, enhance
prognostication, and reﬁne treatment regimens.
In 2018, Ahlqvist et al. (Ahlqvist et al., 2020), in a Scandinavian population (n ¼ 8980), studied six variables (glutamic
acid decarboxylase [GAD] antibody, age, BMI, HbA1c, HOMA- b- (pancreatic b-cell function), and insulin resistance
(HOMA2-IR)), assessed at the time of diagnosis with any form of new-onset diabetes. By employing k-means and hierarchical
clustering algorithms, the study population was classiﬁed into ﬁve reproducible phenotypes: (1) a severe autoimmune
